reason: The text explicitly demonstrates the Israelites freely and directly expressing their complaints and concerns. They vocally quarrel with Moses ('וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־ מֹשֶׁה'), demand water ('תְּנוּ־ לָנוּ מַיִם'), and openly challenge Moses's leadership ('לָמָּה זֶּה הֶעֱלִיתָנוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם'). While Moses questions the legitimacy of their complaints ('מַה־ תְּרִיבוּן עִמָּדִי'), he does not discourage them from speaking. No restriction on expression is imposed; rather, the narrative shows the people as vocally assertive in stating their grievances. The place is even named 'Meribah' (contention) commemorating this very act of expressing dissatisfaction.
